title-group.article-title: γ-Oryzanol Ameliorates Endothelial Replicative Senescence via Downregulation of SGLT2 Expression to Attenuate NADPH-Driven Oxidative Stress

abstract.p: Replicative senescence in endothelial cells is characterized by an irreversible cell cycle arrest and impaired endothelial function, contributing to vascular aging and cardiovascular disease. Natural compounds are being actively studied for their potential to delay cellular senescence and protect vascular health. Among them, rice bran has demonstrated several vascular benefits that are mainly attributed to gamma-oryzanol (γ-Orz), a major bioactive component in rice bran. However, its role in regulating endothelial replicative senescence and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the protective effects of rice bran extract (RBE) and γ-Orz on replicative senescence in porcine coronary artery endothelial cells (PCAECs). Replicative senescence was modeled in PCAECs by serial passaging from P1 to P3 with varying concentrations of RBE and γ-Orz. Senescence was evaluated by measuring senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity, cell proliferation, oxidative stress, and the expression of cell cycle regulatory proteins. RBE and γ-Orz significantly reduced SA-β-gal activity, improved proliferation, and decreased oxidative stress in P3 cells, along with downregulation of senescence-related proteins p53, p21, and p16. Additionally, γ-Orz suppressed sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 expression, reduced NADPH oxidase overexpression, and restored eNOS levels. These findings indicate that RBE and γ-Orz delay endothelial senescence by alleviating oxidative stress, highlighting their potential to reduce cardiovascular disease risk associated with endothelial senescence.

sec.title: INTRODUCTION
sec.p: Aging is a major risk factor in the development of chronic diseases which affect several tissues including the cardiovascular system (North and Sinclair, 2012). Vascular aging, in particular, is characterized by endothelial dysfunction, increased oxidative stress, and arterial stiffness, all of which contributes to pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) such as atherosclerosis, hypertension, stroke and coronary heart disease (Odden et al., 2011; Sun, 2015; Wang and Bennett, 2012). The increasing aging of the global population represents a significant global health challenge in the pathogenesis of CVDs (Yazdanyar and Newman, 2009). Interventions targeting the underlying mechanisms of vascular aging, such as oxidative stress and endothelial senescence, hold promise in preserving vascular health and reducing the incidence of CVDs in the aging population. Therefore, it is a target process to develop a therapeutic strategy to prevent or restore aging related vascular disorders.

Endothelial cells (ECs), which line blood vessels and maintain vascular tone and hemostasis, are highly susceptible to senescence (Sandoo et al., 2010). Cellular senescence is characterized by irreversible cell cycle arrest along with cell enlargement, increased granularity, vacuolization and increased senescence-associated beta galactosidase (SA-β gal) activity (Bode-Boger et al., 2005; Erusalimsky, 2009). However, these cells remain viable and metabolically active (Schafer et al., 2017). It can be induced in vitro by repeated passaging (replicative senescence) or be triggered prematurely by oxidative stress, angiotensin II, high glucose, radiation, and DNA damage (premature senescence) (Kim et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2011; Maeda et al., 2015). Senescence of the vascular cells is the causal path to aging-related endothelial dysfunction and is an important risk factor for the development of CVD such as atherosclerosis, and hypertension (Tian and Li, 2014).

Oxidative stress is a major contributor to ECs senescence and age-related vascular dysfunction (Oeseburg et al., 2010; Touyz and Briones, 2011). Previous studies have indicated that high level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) was observed in aging arteries (Runge et al., 2010), and antioxidants such as vitamin C, and N-acetylcysteine, and polyphenol-rich natural products have shown to improve endothelial function and mitigate age-related dysfunction (Idris Khodja et al., 2012; Khemais-Benkhiat et al., 2016; Monacelli et al., 2017; Voghel et al., 2008). Excessive oxidative burden disrupts nitric oxide signaling by promoting eNOS dysfunction and activating pro-oxidant pathways, including NADPH oxidase-mediated ROS generation (Bhayadia et al., 2016). Recent findings highlight sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) as an additional regulator of vascular redox balance, since its inhibition suppresses ROS production, limits NADPH oxidase activation, and preserves eNOS bioavailability (Dhakal et al., 2023; Tsai et al., 2021; Yaribeygi et al., 2019). These observations suggest that targeting SGLT2-associated oxidative mechanisms may represent a promising strategy to delay endothelial aging.

Currently, numerous interventions are ongoing to develop natural product-based strategies against oxidative stress-induced cellular senescence (Serino and Salazar, 2018). Among these, rice (Oryza sativa L.), a staple cereal crop worldwide, has gained attention. Rice bran, a major byproduct of rice milling process, is rich in bioactive phytochemicals such as γ-oryzanol (γ- Orz), tocopherols, tocotrienols, phytosterols, phenolic acids and flavonoids, which contributes to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cardioprotective properties (Gul et al., 2015; Sohail et al., 2017; Timmerman et al., 2004). In particular, γ- Orz, a mixture of tri-terpene alcohol and phytosterol ferulates possess strong anti-carcinogenic, anti-inflammatory, antihyperlipidemic, and neuroprotective effects, mainly attributed to its significant antioxidant capacity (Minatel et al., 2016). Notably, rice bran enzymatic extracts have shown to reduce oxidative stress and restore endothelial function in obese rats (Justo et al., 2013). Considering the beneficial effects of γ- Orz on endothelial function, γ- Orz could mitigate oxidative stress-induced replicative senescence and help preserve vascular health.

The present study aims to investigate whether rice bran extract (RBE) and its principal bioactive component, γ-Orz, can prevent replicative senescence in endothelial cells (ECs). Using porcine coronary artery endothelial cells (PCAECs), we aim to assess the protective effects of RBE and γ-Orz against redox-sensitive induction of senescence and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms involved.

sec.title: Preparation and standardization of RBE
sec.p: Whole grain rice (1.89 kg) was obtained from Hansalim Consumers Cooperative, which was cultivated and harvested in Boseong-gun, Jeonnam in 2018 (No. P2018RB053-054). It was polished using milling machine (FS-2000, Focus Co.) for isolating bran. The obtained bran (183.9 g) was extracted 70% ethanol at 80°C for 2 h, and concentrated at reduced pressure, and lyophilized to yield the dry extract (15.33 g). The extract was stored at −20°C until use. γ-Orz, a major chemical constituent of RBE, was obtained from Tokyo Chemical Industry. On each experimental day, RBE and γ-Orz were dissolved in the DMSO and treated to the porcine coronary arterial endothelial cell (PCAECs).

sec.title: Analysis of γ-Orz and RBE by HPLC
sec.p: A commercial γ-Orz and RBE extract were analyzed by LC-PDA method to identify chemical composition. The experiments were carried out using a Waters Acquity Arc system (Milford, MA, USA) comprising a Quaternary Solvent Manager-R, a Sample Manager FTN-R, and a 2998 photodiode array detector, and basically operated according to the methods by Xu and Godber (1999) and Cho et al. (2012) (Cho et al., 2012; Xu and Godber, 1999). Each sample (10 μL) was injected onto a Waters SunFireTM C18 (4.6×250 mm, 5 μm) column maintained at 35°C with a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min of acetonitrile/methanol/dichloromethane/acetic acid (55:44:3:1, v/v/v/v). HPLC profiles were recorded at wavelengths ranging between 220 and 500 nm, and each chromatogram was extracted under the same wavelength 320 nm. The retention times (tR) and UV spectra were compared with those of the commercial standard, γ-oryzanol, respectively.

sec.title: Cell culture
sec.p: PCAECs are well established and validated primary cell model for investigating arterial endothelial functions (Lee et al., 2007). To ensure experimental consistency and physiological relevance, pig hearts were collected from the local slaughterhouse immediately after sacrifice and ECs were isolated from the left anterior descending coronary arteries as previously described (Park et al., 2015). The slaughterhouse operates in compliance with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal Cruelty and Slaughter Act guidelines. As the tissues were obtained postmortem from animals processed for commercial food production, the study was not subject to institutional animal care and use protocol approval. Cells were isolated by 1 mg/mL type I collagenase treatment (Worthington Biochemical, Lakewood, NJ, USA) for 12 min at 37°C and cultured in T flasks containing Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), penicillin (100 U/mL), streptomycin (100 U/mL), and fungizone (250 μg/mL) for 48-72 h (passage [P]0). Endothelial identity was verified based on characteristic morphology, including early fusiform growth and the subsequent development of a confluent cobblestone-like monolayer, consistent with established porcine endothelial culture features (Bény and Pacicca, 1994; Budel et al., 2001). In addition, purity and endothelial origin were confirmed by verifying expression of CD34 (Grossini et al., 2012). PCAECs at passage 1 were seeded with 6.0 x 105 cells per T-75 flask for long term treatment. Treatments began after 24 h of seeding. To determine whether RBE and γ-Orz delayed senescence, the cells were treated with final concentrations of RBE (1, 3, 10 µg/mL) and γ-Orz (1, 3, 10 µM) in a total volume of 10 ml of culture medium per flask for 48 h. Then, cells were continuously sub-cultured with equal seeding number until passage P3 in the presence of RBE and γ-Orz. Further experiments were then performed in P3 cells.

sec.title: Detection of senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity
sec.p: Cells were fixed for 10 min in 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS, and incubated for 12 h at 37°C without CO2 with fresh x-gal staining solution [(Citric acid/ NaH2PO4 (1 X), potassium ferricyanide (5 mM), potassium ferrocyanide (5 mM), NaCl (150 mM), MgCl2 (2 mM), X-Gal (1 mg/mL)] (Debacq-Chainiaux et al., 2009). SA-β-gal-positive cells were observed using microscopy, which included counting >300 cells in three independent fields. The percentage of SA-β-gal-positive cells was determined by counting the number of green cells within a sample.

sec.title: Cell proliferation assay
sec.p: Cells were seeded in a 96-well plate at a density of 1×104 cells/well and cultured for 12 h in 10% FBS/DMEM. Afterwards, different concentrations of RBE and γ-Orz were treated for 48 h in 10% FBS/DMEM. After adding 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyl tetrazolium bromide (MTT) (0.1 mg/mL) for 4 h, formazan crystals that had formed were solubilized in 100 μL dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO) and the absorbance was measured at 540 nm.

sec.title: Measurement of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in PCAECs
sec.p: Cells were seeded at a concentration of 5×104 cells/well in 6 well plates and allowed to adhere overnight. Cells were then treated with various concentrations of RBE and γ-Orz for 24 h. Intracellular ROS levels were evaluated by fluorescence microscopy. The redox-sensitive fluorescent dye dihydroethidium (DHE) was used to evaluate the in-situ formation of ROS. DHE dissolved in DMSO was added to cells at 10 μM. After incubation for 30 min at 37°C under a 5% CO2 atmosphere, the cells washed with PBS were visualized under a fluorescence microscope and images were acquired and signal intensity measured using Image J software.

sec.title: Western blot
sec.p: Cells were homogenized and lysed in radio-immunoprecipitation assay buffer (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), supplemented with protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Sigma-Aldrich). The cell lysate was centrifuged at 13000 rpm at 4°C for 20 min. The supernatant was collected and quantified using an albumin standard (GenDEPOT, Katy, TX, USA) and DC protein assay reagent (Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA, USA). A total of 15 µg per well of protein was boiled with 1× loading buffer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA; cat. no. 39000) for 10 min. The protein was loaded onto a 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel and separated by electrophoresis, then transferred to a polyvinylidene difluoride membrane that was blocked with 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) for 1 h and incubated overnight at 4°C with primary antibodies against β-actin (sc-47778, 1:5000; Santa Cruz Biotechnology); p53 (sc-6243, 1:1000; Santa Cruz Biotechnology); p21 (sc-397, 1:1000; Santa Cruz Biotechnology); p16 (sc-1661, 1:1000; Santa Cruz Biotechnology); p22phox (sc-271968, 1:1000; Santa Cruz Biotechnology); SGLT2 (AGT-032, 1:1000, Alomone labs); eNOS (cat. no. 610297, 1:1000; BD biosciences); NOX2 (cat. no. 19013-1-AP, 1:1000; Protein tech); diluted in 5% BSA. After washing, the membrane was incubated with horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (cat. no. 7074S, 1:10,000; Cell Signaling Technology) or HRP-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (cat no. 7076S, 1:2000; Cell Signaling Technology), then washed and treated with enhanced chemiluminescence substrate (GE Healthcare, Little Chalfont, UK; cat. no. RPN2232) and visualized with a chemiluminescence system (UVItec, Cambridge, UK).

sec.title: Statistical analysis
sec.p: Data are expressed as mean ± standard error of means (SEM). Statistical analysis was carried out via one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with a Tukey post hoc test. A p<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

sec.title: RBE delayed replicative senescence of PCAECs
sec.p: Previous studies have indicated that serial passaging of PCAECs (P1-P3) resulted in the induction of senescence (Khemais-Benkhiat et al., 2016). To investigate whether RBE delays replicative ECs senescence, serial passaging of ECs from P1 to P3 was conducted in presence of RBE. ECs senescence was assessed using SA-β-gal activity by detection of x-gal staining. Compared with P1 ECs, P3 cells exhibited a marked increase in the proportion of SA-β-gal–positive (senescent) cells. Treatment with RBE significantly reduced SA-β-gal activity in P3 ECs in a concentration-dependent manner, indicating that RBE effectively delays replicative senescence in endothelial cells (Fig. 1A, 1B).

Cell cycle arrest is a hallmark of aging, characterized by a limited number of cell divisions and reduced proliferative capacity (Ben-Porath and Weinberg, 2005; Burger et al., 2012). To determine whether RBE prevents senescence-induced reduction in ECs proliferation, we assessed proliferation in early-passage (P1) and late-passage (P3) cells. In line with the senescent phenotype, the proliferative capacity of P3 ECs was markedly reduced compared with P1 ECs. Notably, RBE treatment increased the proliferative potential of P3 ECs (Fig. 1C). These findings indicate that RBE delays cellular senescence and counteracts the senescence-associated decline in EC proliferation.

Overproduction of ROS has been reported as a key trigger of both premature and replicative endothelial senescence (Khemais-Benkhiat et al., 2016). It is also well established that ameliorating oxidative stress is one of the key strategies to delay senescence (Sharma et al., 2019). To investigate whether RBE decreases oxidative stress-associated replicative senescence, ROS level was measured with DHE staining, a widely used fluorescent probe that specifically detects superoxide anions and provides a reliable assessment of intracellular oxidative stress (Olowe et al., 2020). P3 ECs showed increase in oxidative stress, as indicated by increase in DHE fluorescence. Notably, treatment with RBE attenuated this effect and significantly reduced ROS levels in a concentration dependent manner (Fig. 1D, 1E). This suggests that RBE may possess potent antioxidant components that contribute to the prevention of replicative senescence.

sec.title: Comparison of γ-Orz and RBE by HPLC analysis
sec.p: To characterize the chemical composition of γ-Orz, HPLC analysis was performed using a commercial γ-Orz standard. The chromatogram revealed four major ferulate esters: cycloartenyl ferulate (1, tR 19.42), 24-methylenecycloartanyl ferulate (2, tR 21.31), campesteryl ferulate (3, tR 22.93), and β-sitosteryl ferulate (4, tR 25.92) (Fig. 2A). These findings are consistent with previous reports describing the characteristic composition of γ-Orz (Cho et al., 2012). Similarly, RBE extract was subjected to the same chromatographic analysis, and peaks corresponding to the same four compounds were identified (Fig. 2B). The retention times of the peaks detected in RBE were consistent with those of the commercial γ-Orz standard, and their UV absorption spectra closely matched the corresponding peaks in the standard γ-Orz, further confirming the identity of the detected ferulate esters (Fig. 2C). Structural assignments of these four compounds are presented in Fig. 2D.

sec.title: γ-Orz, a bioactive component of RBE, delayed replicative senescence and inhibited oxidative stress
sec.p: To examine whether γ-Orz, a bioactive component of RBE, can prevent replicative senescence in PCAECs, serial passaging of ECs from P1 to P3 was conducted in presence of γ-Orz. Treatment with γ-Orz significantly reduced SA-β-gal activity in P3 ECs as indicated by x-gal staining (Fig. 3A, 3B). In addition, γ-Orz increased the proliferative capacity of P3 ECs, indicating its ability to counteract the senescence-associated decline in cell proliferation (Fig. 3C).

γ-Orz, a phenolic compound abundantly present in RBE, has been widely reported as a potent antioxidant (Minatel et al., 2016). To evaluate whether γ-Orz reduces oxidative stress in senescent ECs, P1 ECs were cultured with different concentrations of γ-Orz followed by serial passaging until P3. Intracellular ROS levels were then assessed using DHE staining. P3 ECs showed increased oxidative stress compared to P1 ECs, as indicated by increased DHE fluorescence. Treatment with γ-Orz decreased ROS overproduction in a concentration dependent manner in P3 ECs (Fig. 3D, 3E). This suggests that γ-Orz has potent antioxidant effect and may prevent oxidative stress- induced replicative senescence in ECs.

sec.title: RBE and γ-Orz prevented senescence-associated upregulation of cell cycle regulatory proteins
sec.p: During replicative senescence, ECs undergoes cell cycle arrest by upregulating expression of cell cycle regulatory proteins such as p53, p16 and p21 (Matthaei et al., 2012; Mirzayans et al., 2012; Rosso et al., 2006). Consistent with this, P3 ECs exhibited markedly elevated levels of p53, p16, and p21 compared to P1 ECs, confirming their role in senescence-associated growth arrest. Treatment with RBE significantly suppressed the expression of these cell cycle regulators in P3 ECs (Fig. 4A-4D), thereby enhancing their proliferative potential. Similarly, γ-Orz treatment also led to a marked reduction in p53, p16, and p21 expression (Fig. 5A-5D), further supporting its ability to counteract senescence-associated cell cycle arrest. Collectively, these findings indicate that both RBE and γ-Orz protect against replicative senescence through suppression of cell cycle regulatory proteins, thereby helping to preserve endothelial proliferative capacity. Given that γ-Orz is a major bioactive constituent of RBE and reproduced these protective effects, we next explored the mechanistic actions of γ-Orz to gain deeper insight into how it mediates endothelial protection against replicative senescence.

sec.title: γ-Orz downregulates sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) expression and attenuates NADPH oxidase-mediated oxidative stress
sec.p: To determine whether γ-Orz regulates redox-associated senescence mechanisms, we examined the expression of SGLT2, NADPH oxidase subunits, and eNOS expression in aged ECs. Senescent P3 ECs exhibited a marked upregulation of SGLT2 expression, which was significantly reduced by γ-Orz treatment (Fig. 6A, 6B). γ-Orz also suppressed the expression of NADPH oxidase subunits NOX2 and p22phox, which are key contributors to ROS production in endothelial cells (Fig. 6C, 6D). In addition to the observed decrease in NADPH oxidase expression, there was a notable increase in the expression of eNOS in γ-Orz treated ECs (Fig.6A-6E). Collectively, these results suggest that downregulation of SGLT2 expression by γ-Orz reduced NADPH oxidase activity, thereby reducing oxidative stress and enhancing eNOS expression, which together contributes to improved endothelial function during replicative senescence (Fig. 7).

sec.title: DISCUSSION
sec.p: The present study investigated the role of RBE and its major component, γ-Orz in replicative senescence in vitro. The results demonstrated that both RBE and γ-Orz significantly delayed replicative endothelial senescence, as indicated by decreased SA-β- gal activity as well as reduced cell cycle regulatory proteins, such as p53, p21 and p16 expression. In addition, γ-Orz suppressed the progressive upregulation of SGLT2, NADPH oxidase subunits p22phox and NOX2, reduced ROS levels, and restored eNOS expression. Overall, these findings suggest that γ-Orz could be promising candidate against endothelial aging, capable of preserving vascular function and delaying the onset of cellular senescence.

In this study, we used PCAECs as an in vitro model of coronary endothelial aging. Pigs more closely resemble humans than rodents in cardiovascular anatomy and physiology, making them superior models for cardiovascular research (Jia et al., 2024). Their coronary vasculature closely resembles human coronary circulation in terms of vessel size, function, and endothelial phenotype (Lelovas et al., 2014; Santos et al., 2015). In addition, pigs develop human-like atherosclerosis and exhibit endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress in response to classical cardiovascular risk factors, making them highly suitable for translational cardiovascular research (Turk et al., 2005). Therefore, the anti-senescent and vasculoprotective effects of γ-Orz observed in PCAECs are likely to have strong translational relevance to human endothelial aging and coronary artery disease.

This study showed that RBE and γ-Orz delayed EC senescence as evidenced by the reduction of SA-β-gal activity in P3 ECs. SA-β-gal activity reflects aging of ECs and serves as a marker for senescence (Debacq-Chainiaux et al., 2009). During replicative senescence, ECs undergo cell cycle arrest which ultimately lead to limited number of cell divisions and the decrease in proliferation (Ben-Porath and Weinberg, 2005; Burger et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2015). In our study, RBE and γ-Orz promoted EC proliferation in P3 senescent cells which suggests that RBE and γ-Orz might prevent senescence- associated cell cycle arrest. These effects were accompanied by marked reduction in the expression of cell cycle regulatory proteins including p53, p21, and p16. p53 is activated by DNA damage, telomere dysfunction, and senescence. It activates the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor, p21 which inhibits cell proliferation (Rosso et al., 2006). Similarly, p16 is a member of the inhibitors of CDK4 protein family that acts through the Rb pathway to cause cell cycle arrest and lead to cellular senescence (Bhayadia et al., 2016). Reduced expression of these proteins suggests that RBE and γ-Orz delay endothelial senescence by suppressing the p53-p21 and p16-Rb pathways, which helps preserve proliferative capacity and maintain normal cell cycle progression.

Oxidative stress is recognized as a key mechanism in the induction of ECs senescence (Oeseburg et al., 2010; Touyz and Briones, 2011). It has been demonstrated that γ-Orz also has ROS scavenging potency which has been attributed to its ferulic acid moieties that acts as effective ROS scavengers (Juliano et al., 2005). Similarly, RBE, which is rich in phenolic compounds, has been reported to exert strong antioxidant effects that can ameliorate vascular aging and improve endothelial function (Arab et al., 2011). In this study, both RBE and its active constituent, γ-Orz demonstrated pronounced antioxidant activity by attenuating ROS generation and restoring redox homeostasis. Therefore, it could play a critical role in delaying oxidative stress-induced replicative senescence of ECs and ultimately contribute to the preservation of vascular health. The antioxidant and endothelial protective effects observed by RBE might be attributed to its principal bioactive component, γ-Orz. Initially regarded as single compound, γ-Orz is now considered as heterogenous mixture of phytosteryl ferulates, cycloartenyl ferulate, 24-methylenecycloartanyl ferulate, campesteryl ferulate, and β-sitosteryl ferulate identified as the predominant constituents, collectively accounting for nearly 80% of the total content in rice bran oil (Juliano et al., 2005; Xu and Godber, 1999). To verify its chemical composition, HPLC analysis was performed using a commercial γ-Orz standard, which revealed four characteristic ferulate esters- cycloartenyl ferulate, 24-methylenecycloartanyl ferulate, campesteryl ferulate, and β-sitosteryl ferulate. A similar profile was observed in RBE, confirming that γ-Orz is a principal constituent of the RBE.

Recent studies have increasingly linked SGLT2 inhibition to the attenuation of oxidative stress associated with cellular senescence, highlighting its therapeutic potential beyond glycemic control (Yesilyurt-Dirican et al., 2025). For instance, Katsuumi et al. demonstrated that SGLT2 inhibition significantly reduces oxidative stress in senescent cells (Katsuumi et al., 2024). Mechanistically, SGLT2 inhibitors mitigate senescence-associated oxidative stress through multiple pathways, including inhibition of NADPH oxidase, activation of the NRF2/SIRT1 axis, and enhanced clearance of senescent cells (Dhakal et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2021). These mechanisms collectively preserve vascular and renal function, highlighting their role in aging-related pathologies. Several specific SGLT2 inhibitors have shown promising anti-senescent effects in preclinical models. Dagliflozin, one of the SGLT2 inhibitors have been shown to delay organ aging and enhance learning and memory capabilities in aged mice (Ma et al., 2023). Moreover, both empagliflozin and dapagliflozin have been reported to reverse endothelial cell senescence and dysfunction indicating a vasculoprotective effect (Madonna et al., 2022). Notably, several natural medicines rich in polyphenols have also been identified as natural modulators of SGLT2 (Borah et al., 2022). As γ-Orz is a polyphenol-rich phytochemical, its potential to regulate SGLT2 may underlie its anti-senescent actions. Given this context, we explored whether the protective effects of γ-Orz against oxidative stress-induced replicative senescence in endothelial cells are associated with modulation of SGLT2 expression. Increased SGLT2 expression in P3 cells were significantly downregulated by γ-Orz treatment suggesting that oxidative potential of γ-Orz might be associated with SGLT2 modulation.

Current evidence indicates that ROS-generating enzymes are causal link between the excess formation of ROS and EC senescence (Schilder et al., 2009). Among these, activation of pro-oxidant enzymes such as NADPH oxidase is a major source of ROS in senescent human endothelial cells and, genetic knockdown or pharmacological blocking of these enzymes delayed senescence in ECs (Lener et al., 2009). In line with this, P3 ECs exhibited a marked upregulation of NADPH oxidase subunits p22phox and NOX2, which likely enhanced ROS production and exacerbated oxidative stress within the endothelium. The elevated ROS levels not only contribute to cellular damage but also promote eNOS uncoupling, shifting its function from producing NO to generate superoxide, further amplifying oxidative stress (Łuczak et al., 2020). Consistently, reduced eNOS expression was observed in P3 ECs, further compromising NO bioavailability and endothelial function. γ-Orz treatment markedly suppressed NADPH oxidase expression, reducing ROS production and oxidative stress while restoring eNOS expression. Notably, this reduction in NOX2 and p22phox expression was accompanied by decreased SGLT2 levels, suggesting that γ-Orz may attenuate NADPH oxidase–mediated oxidative stress at least in part, through modulation of SGLT2 expression. Several studies have shown that pharmacological SGLT2 inhibitors not only block transporter activity but also downregulate SGLT2 expression at the mRNA and protein levels (Eleftheriadis et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2021). In this context, the observation that γ-Orz reduces SGLT2 expression suggests that its effect may similarly translate into decreased SGLT2 activity and attenuation of downstream oxidative signaling during endothelial senescence. Taken together, these findings suggest that γ-Orz mitigates endothelial senescence by modulating SGLT2 expression and restoring redox balance, underscoring its therapeutic potential for vascular aging and related diseases.

This study has some limitations. While the findings demonstrate that γ-Orz restores eNOS expression and suppresses NADPH oxidase subunits, thereby reducing ROS production, these results still indicate a potential mechanistic involvement rather than a definitive pathway. Direct confirmation would require further studies using genetic knockdown/knockout of SGLT2 or NADPH oxidase, or pathway-specific inhibitors. Moreover, the present work demonstrates only in vitro efficacy, and validation in relevant in vivo model of senescence will be necessary to strengthen the translational impact. Additionally, this study did not include a known SGLT2 inhibitor as a positive control; however, several studies have shown that agents such as dapagliflozin and empagliflozin exert similar antioxidant and endothelial-protective effects, supporting the plausibility of our proposed SGLT2-dependent mechanism (Katsuumi et al., 2024; Mone et al., 2022; Park et al., 2021). These findings align with evidence that SGLT2 inhibition preserves endothelial function by reducing ROS generation and maintaining eNOS-derived NO bioavailability (Yesilyurt-Dirican et al. 2025; Dhakal et al., 2023). Importantly, future studies directly comparing γ-Orz with classical SGLT2 inhibitors will be valuable to further clarify their relative efficacy and underlying mechanisms of action. Despite these limitations, this study demonstrates that downregulation of SGLT2 expression by γ-Orz suppresses NADPH oxidase, leading to reduced oxidative stress. This effect restores eNOS expression, which may contribute to improved endothelial function. Overall, these findings highlight γ-Orz as a potential therapeutic candidate for vascular complications associated with endothelial senescence.

Graphical abstract illustrating the protective effects of γ-Orz against replicative senescence in PCAECs. γ-Orz suppresses SGLT2 expression, leading to reduced NADPH oxidase-mediated ROS production, restoration of eNOS levels, and inhibition of the p53/p21/p16 signaling pathway. These effects collectively decrease SA-β-gal activity, improve cell proliferation, and delay ECs senescence, thereby contributing to the mitigation of vascular aging. Abbreviations: γ-Orz, γ-oryzanol; PCAECs, porcine coronary artery endothelial cells; SGLT2, sodium-glucose co-transporter 2; NADPH oxidase, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase; ROS, reactive oxygen species; eNOS, endothelial nitric oxide synthase; SA-β-gal, senescence-associated beta-galactosidase; ECs, endothelial cells.
